LRIC and cross-PCF — the spatial co-occurrence branch

scripts/comparators/liana/run_lric.py → results/comparators/liana/GBM/lric_percore/, following LRIC_tutorial.ipynb. Neither function had been called before in this project. This is the only branch in the whole LIANA+ pass that resolves direction (sender → receiver) as an explicit argument rather than as part of a feature name.

What the two functions compute

li.mt.cross_pcf is the classical cross pair-correlation function g(r). For an ordered cell-type pair (A → B) and an annulus [r, r+w) it counts the B cells falling in that annulus around each A cell, and divides by the count expected under complete spatial randomness at the observed density. g = 1 means "no more co-located than chance". The expected count uses n_points / bounding-box area, with a per-annulus edge correction that computes the fraction of each ring lying inside the bounding box (_circle_bbox_fractions, sampled at n_angle_samples=360). Neither function consumes a connectivity graph; both build their own cKDTree.

li.mt.lric is the same estimator with the cells weighted by expression — senders by the ligand, receivers by the receptor, each mean-normalised to 1 so an all-equal weighting reduces to cross-PCF exactly. The LRIC / cross-PCF ratio is therefore the whole point of the branch: it asks whether ligand/receptor expression adds anything over where the cells happen to sit. A ratio of 1 means the co-occurrence is fully explained by cell-type co-location.

Neither li.mt.lric nor li.mt.cross_pcf consumes a connectivity graph — they build their own cKDTree from the coordinates. The repo's 13.1454 µm bandwidth is therefore irrelevant to this branch, and harmonising it in would have been the deviation, not omitting it. This branch is consequently exempt from contract deviation CD-1, and the exemption is recorded in the manifest under why_per_punch.spatial_neighbors_not_called rather than being left as an inference.

Results: one directional positive, one non-replication, one clean negative

Punches, not cells, are the replicate unit throughout. First, can the test even run? mGAM clears min_cells=50 in 11 / 13 punches (failures: punch 2 with 13 mGAM cells, punch 6 with 2 — both low grade). min_expressing=20 removes more. Every missing number is attributed to a specific gate in combined/target_availability.csv; that file is a design feature, not a footnote.

Result 1 — direction asymmetry holds for GRN→SORT1, and does not hold for ANXA1→FPR1.

Result 2 — the LRIC / cross-PCF ratio is ~1 everywhere. This is a negative result and is reported as one. Per-punch median ratios: GRN^SORT1 mGAM→MES-like 1.043 (Wilcoxon vs 1, p = 0.383), MES-like→mGAM 0.963 (p = 0.109); ANXA1^FPR1 mGAM→MES-like 1.040 (p = 0.438), MES-like→mGAM 1.033 (p = 0.313). All four p > 0.10. Per bin the median ratio stays inside 0.93–1.13 everywhere except one dip (GRN^SORT1 MES-like→mGAM in [50,75) at 0.785).

So the spatial co-occurrence LIANA reports for these pairs is fully explained by cell-type co-location plus the underlying point pattern; ligand and receptor expression contribute nothing detectable. A useful corollary: this also refutes the "the 28.2 µm kernel was too narrow and missed a longer-range interaction" explanation — the ratio is ~1 in every annulus out to 225 µm, eight times the bivariate/inflow support radius. There is no longer-range LR-specific structure for a wider kernel to have found.

Result 3 — grade is not testable in this branch, and the loss is systematic. Of the 8 punches supporting GRN^SORT1, 7 are high grade (1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 11, 13) and exactly 1 is low grade (punch 9). That is not random attrition: the low-grade punches are precisely the ones where mGAM falls below min_cells (punches 2, 6) or MES-like GRN+/SORT1+/ANXA1+/FPR1+ falls below min_expressing (punches 4, 12, 14 — MES-like SORT1+ = 7 / 15 / 7, GRN+ = 7 / 5 / 3). n = 7 vs 1 supports no test, and none was run. The cell-type-agnostic fallback (13/13 punches for GRN^SORT1) gives Mann-Whitney p = 0.234 and p = 0.788 — no grade difference, and its direction should not be read, because the low-grade punches pushing the agnostic median up are the small, sparse ones.

LR-MISTy — multi-view modelling

scripts/comparators/liana/run_misty.py → results/comparators/liana/GBM/misty/linear_fullslide/, following the Ligand-Receptor MISTy section of misty.ipynb.

The call, as run

    --h5ad data/xenium_mm_final_cell_id.h5ad \
    --cellchatdb data/LRdatabase/CellChatDBv2.0.human.csv \
    --outdir results/comparators/liana/GBM/misty/linear_fullslide --model linear

misty = lrMistyData(adata,                     # tutorial: adata[:, hvg]  -- see DEV-1
                    resource=cellchatdb,       # tutorial: resource_name="consensus"
                    bandwidth=200.0,           # TUTORIAL value (package default 100)
                    set_diag=False,            # tutorial value = package default
                    cutoff=0.01,               # TUTORIAL value (package default 0.1)
                    nz_threshold=0.1,          # tutorial value = package default
                    kernel="misty_rbf",        # package default; tutorial does not override
                    zoi=0.0)
# intra view 100,190 x 382 receptor TARGETS ; extra view 100,190 x 37 ligand PREDICTORS
misty(model=LinearModel, bypass_intra=True, predict_self=False, k_cv=10, seed=1337, verbose=True)
# 0.423 s/target x 382 = 2.69 min fit; 2.91 min wall; peak RSS 6.12 GB

Two structural facts that determine how the output must be read, both verified in the installed source rather than inferred:

  • bypass_intra=True means gain_R2 is not a gain. _Misty.py sets intra_r2 = ... if not bypass_intra else 0, so intra_R2 is 0.0 for all 379 non-NaN rows and gain_R2 == multi_R2 exactly. It is the cross-validated R² of the ligand extra view alone, with nothing subtracted. The question "does the spatial view add anything over an intrinsic model" is never computed by the tutorial configuration.
  • With one view the contribution column is 1.0 by construction — the meta-model coefficient is normalised to itself, so contributions.csv reads extra = 1.0 for every target. Uninformative by design, not broken.

Deviations from misty.ipynb

But the consequence must be reported: at bandwidth=200, cutoff=0.01 the nominal support is 200·√(−2·ln 0.01) = 607.0 µm, which is 2.7× the 222.9 µm inter-core cell floor, and there are genuine cross-core edges — 2,520 of 10,119,190 (0.0249%), touching 232 of 100,190 cells. What contains the damage is max_neighbours=100, which lrMistyData does not expose: degree median = max = 100, the cap binds for 99.7% of cells, so the extra view is in practice a 100-NN neighbourhood rather than a 200 µm kernel. Undocumented in the tutorial; found by inspection.
HVG pre-step adata[:, hvg] applied, framed as "for the sake of computational speed" omitted — full panel used Measured, not argued (--hvg 1 --n-top-genes 1521 --construct-only 1, kept as misty/hvg_probe_construct_only/): on the full slide HVG gives intra 100,190 × 82 / extra 100,190 × 13, against 382 / 37 without it — 78% of receptor targets and 65% of ligand predictors discarded. On one 5,363-cell punch it collapses the extra view to a single ligand predictor (intra 5363 × 54, extra 5363 × 1), which makes the model vacuous. The tutorial's own justification is speed, on a genome-wide Visium slide; this is a 5,119-gene targeted panel where HVG removes signal rather than noise, and the full-panel fit takes 2.7 minutes.

The motif-1 negative it produced was therefore uninformative — the model could not have found what was not in the extra view. On the full slide both clear the gate (GRN 10.88%, ANXA1 12.06%), so the full-slide run is a fair test. Fitting per core would give 13 incomparable models, each with its own nz_threshold-determined predictor set.

The 21 control probes contain _, which is LIANA's heteromeric-subunit separator. ⚠️ run_liana.py's bivariate branch skips this QC, which is why that branch has 100,197 cells against this run's 100,190 — cross-branch joins must be on cell ID, never on position.

Results, and the honest read

Over 382 targets: median gain_R2 0.00414, 133 / 382 (34.8%) exceed 0.01, 20 exceed 0.05, max 0.577 (MET). 57 targets are exactly 0 (a negative mean CV R² clipped at 0 — the ultra-sparse receptors) and 3 are NaN (heteromeric complexes whose elementwise-min is constant zero, so the variance is 0; liana logs this itself).

For the two required LRIs:

targetgain_R2rankGRN as predictorANXA1 as predictor
SORT10.062117 / 382t = +5.46, rank 9 / 37t = −3.50, rank 11 / 37 (wrong sign)
FPR10.026254 / 382t = +7.08, 3rd strongest of 37t = +1.34, rank 22 / 37 — does not replicate

The honest read: this is shared spatial context, not LR mechanism. Three concrete reasons, and the third is decisive:

  1. The best target in the whole model is reconstructed without its own ligand. MET (R² = 0.577) is predicted from THY1 (t = −38.1), TNR (+32.0), TNC (+28.8), NTN1 (−27.0) and CD99 (−25.0). HGF — MET's cognate ligand — is absent from the model entirely: it is non-zero in only 3.77% of cells and fails nz_threshold=0.1. The model reconstructs MET from a mesenchymal/glial neighbourhood signature.
  2. Nothing is subtracted (bypass_intra=True), so gain_R2 cannot separate "spatial ligand information" from "anything correlated with position".
  3. The extra view is 37 ligands wide out of 3,218 CellChatDB pairs, and the 100-NN cap binds for 99.7% of cells. What is being regressed is a heavily smoothed 100-cell neighbourhood average of 37 abundant genes — a niche-composition proxy.

So LR-MISTy's gain_R2 ranking must not be read as an LRI ranking. This branch is also the one LIANA branch that contributes no grade result, by design: it returns a cross-validated R² per target, not per cell or per core, so there is no quantity to aggregate to the 13 punches and no native contrast in the package. run_misty.py reads tma_id only to report per-group cell counts.

The punch-level grade test — a documented substitute, not a native mode

The benchmark contract (.claude/skills/comparator-benchmark/SKILL.md:47-49) requires the method's native multi-sample / differential mode, with obs['grade'] as the contrast and the 13 obs['tma_id'] cores as the units. What the inflow branch actually ran was li.mt.compute_global_specificity(groupby='grade'). Reading the installed implementation, that is a one-sided per-group specificity test which permutes labels across cells. It is not a contrast: region_global_interactions.csv is 9,216 rows = 4,608 × 2 (one block for high, one for low), with no contrast column, no effect size and no direction.

The replicate-unit problem, made concrete. Those permutations run over n = 100,190 cells against 13 punches — roughly 7,700× pseudoreplication. That is why 5,417 rows come out at p < 0.05 in global_interactions.csv. Those p-values are a ranking statistic, not evidence of a grade difference, and every quotation of them has to say so.

analyse_existing.py therefore does the contrast at the units the design actually has. It is read-only on the existing run and re-fits nothing (0.12 min wall):

/Users/jiayifan/anaconda3/envs/comp-liana/bin/python scripts/comparators/liana/analyse_existing.py \
    --nmf-dir results/comparators/liana/GBM/nmf_inflow \
    --inflow-dir results/comparators/liana/GBM/cellchatdb2_inflow \
    --h5ad data/xenium_mm_final_cell_id.h5ad \
    --out-dir results/comparators/liana/GBM/nmf_inflow/punch_level

W = np.load(".../nmf_inflow/data/nmf_WH.npz")["W"]          # (100190, 7) cells x factors
# cell order is ASSERTED against cell_meta.csv, not assumed; the script exits if it differs
punch = pd.DataFrame(W, columns=factors).assign(punch=tma_id).groupby("punch").mean()   # 13 rows
u, p = mannwhitneyu(punch[high], punch[low], alternative="two-sided")   # n = 7 vs 6 PUNCHES
q = benjamini_hochberg(p)
# and the floor, printed on every run:
#   2 / comb(13, 6) = 0.0011655  -- the smallest two-sided p this design can produce

The same aggregation was applied to the 20 required-LR inflow features (9 senders × 2 LRs + 2 aggregates) and, inside run_mofaflex.py, to the MOFA-Flex factor scores.

Note the hard floor: a two-sided rank test on 7 vs 6 units cannot go below p = 0.0011655, so this design has little power and the null result is weak evidence of absence, not evidence of no effect. The gap between "0 significant at n = 13" and "5,417 significant at n = 100,190" is the pseudoreplication, made concrete.

This does not close the contract gap, and must not be presented as if it did. SKILL.md:49 says verbatim: "If the method has no multi-sample mode, say so — do not hand-roll one." LIANA has no native spatial differential mode, so the requirement is inapplicable and is marked N/A, not satisfied. The punch-level test is recorded as an additional analysis of ours. grep -n by_sample scripts/comparators/liana/*.py returns nothing — none of by_sample, dotplot_by_sample, lrs_to_views or to_tensor_c2c was ever called.

Defects found by audit, and what they cost

These are recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the tally matters more than any individual bug: a plausible, quotable, wrong result survived at least one full documentation pass before being caught — twice.

#DefectCauseFix
1 Row-order misalignment corrupted the SENDER and LR-pair axes in plot_liana_full.py. Affected 2 CSVs and 8 figures: factor_by_SENDER_celltype.csv, factor_by_LRpair.csv, heatmap_factor_by_SENDER.png, heatmap_factor_by_LRpair_top30.png, celltype_communication_by_factor.png, identity_Factor1..7.png (inflow) and 2 files in the bivariate tree. Not one of the 7 inflow factors had the right top sender. li.ut.get_variable_loadings re-sorts by |Factor 1| descending. The script built its annotation vectors (sender_of, lr_of) from nmf_WH.npz but its value vectors from NMF_H_loadings.csv, then masked one by the other — pairing each feature's name with a different feature's loading. The two orderings agreed at 0 of 2,704 positions (inflow) and 1 of 131 (bivariate). A pure permutation: the underlying fit was never wrong. The corruption was visible inside a single figure — identity_Factor1.png showed ten Glial-Neuronal^… bars under a suptitle reading "top sender: AC-like". Reindex once immediately after load (loadings = loadings.loc[list(feats)]), assert the alignment, raise if any npz feature is missing from the CSV. Both trees regenerated. ⚠️ METHODS.md's prose sender list is right — it came from top10_loadings_per_factor.csv, not from the broken figures; it must not be "corrected" to match them.
2 Four blank PNGs across three scripts: nmf_{bivariate,inflow}/plots_full/global/connectivity.png (6,365 bytes, one unique colour, mean pixel 255.0) and mofaflex_inflow{,/sensitivity_nzf0.001}/plots/dotplot_focus_factors.png (4,377 bytes, all white). The same plotnine return-type trap in all four. li.pl.connectivity and li.pl.dotplot return a plotnine ggplot and never touch the matplotlib state; the code saved plt.gcf(), an empty canvas. No exception was raised, so the scripts' try/except guards logged "ok" and the blank files were written. The correct idiom already existed 200 lines away in run_inflow_downstream.py, complete with an inline comment naming the trap. A first pixel audit over ~140 PNGs caught only the two connectivity.png; the two dotplots were found later, which is how we know that audit was not exhaustive. return_fig=True + gg.save(...) through a plotnine-aware saver, plus a _is_blank() detector in every saver that refuses to write a canvas with no drawn content and names the trap in the failure message. Final sweep: 420 PNGs across the LIANA tree, 0 blank. Impact was cosmetic — nothing downstream reads these figures.
3 The k_range confound — the default-tier NMF fits were compared against cellchatdb2 fits on a different rank-selection window, producing a quotable but unattributable "the LR database changes the factor count" claim. run_default_tier.sh called run_nmf.py without --k-max, whose default is 11, so the default tier searched 1..10 while cellchatdb2 searched 1..20. Kneedle normalises the elbow curve over the window it is given, so ranks from different windows are not comparable — a trap this repo had already documented. Cross-referenced in full in the NMF section. Both default-tier NMFs refitted with --k-max 21; the script now passes it explicitly with a comment saying why it must never be omitted. On the matched window the headline does not survive: bivariate 6 → 6 (despite tripling the feature count), inflow 7 → 5.
4 A replot clobbered MOFA-Flex fit provenance. Both manifests came to record fit_seconds: null, determinism_probe: null, and a wall_seconds / peak_rss_gb describing the replot (73.6 s / 3.24 GB primary, 81.5 s / 4.24 GB sensitivity). The Defect-2 regeneration pass reloaded the cached model (refit: false) and rewrote the manifest wholesale. The 70.5 min fit, 76.0 min wall, 4.1 GB peak, the stopping epochs 632 / 199 and the determinism probe survived only in logs/mofaflex_{primary,sensitivity}.log. The manifest had never recorded the stopping epoch at all. Restored from those logs — the only surviving source — and each manifest carries a provenance_note saying so rather than pretending the values were remeasured. run_mofaflex.py now carries fit_seconds / n_epochs / determinism_probe / peak_rss_gb / wall_seconds forward on a cached-model replot and records the replot separately under last_replot.
5 run_inflow.py was truncated. It ended after li.mt.inflow, created an empty plots/ directory, and never ran the five downstream steps of inflow_score.ipynb. Without compute_global_specificity the branch had no source→target significance at all. Nothing errored — the calls were simply absent. The gap survived until someone noticed the empty plots/ directory. Cross-referenced in full in the inflow section. run_inflow_downstream.py now performs all five (compute_global_specificity in its cell-type, region and cell_type::region variants, spatial_pair_proximity, and the spatially-constrained rank_aggregate) and produces 80 figures, 0 blank.

What made these possible

  • Exception-swallowing guards. plot_liana_full.py's guard() caught and logged rather than raised, so any figure it silently skipped leaves no file and no trace. The four blank PNGs are the cases we caught, and only because a blank file is visible on disk. We cannot now determine whether anything else failed and was swallowed.
  • Missing invocations and logs. The command lines that produced the on-disk plots_full/ trees were recorded nowhere and had to be reconstructed from the manifests in order to regenerate. There is still no log for the original run_liana.py / run_inflow.py / run_nmf.py fits. Manifests now record script, input, out_dir, required_lrs, git_sha, wall_min and two fix-confirmation flags (blank_figures_suppressed, loadings_reindexed_to_npz_order), but still no literal argv in most.
  • 🔴 Still open: scripts/comparators/ is not tracked in git. git ls-files scripts/comparators returns nothing, and it is not ignored either — it has simply never been added. Every manifest records git_sha: 95208de, which pins the package, not the comparator scripts that produced the results. An edit can be confirmed to have the intended content, but there is no way to prove no other line moved, and no way to tie a manifest to the script revision that wrote it. This is the largest remaining reproducibility hole in this comparator.

figures.caption: The central negative result of the LRIC branch. The LRIC/cross-PCF ratio for GRN→SORT1 and ANXA1→FPR1, per punch, plotted against annulus distance: it sits on 1 in every bin out to 225 µm (per-punch medians 0.963–1.043, all Wilcoxon-vs-1 p > 0.10). Expression adds nothing over cell-type co-location — and because the flat line extends to 225 µm, eight times the bivariate/inflow support radius, there is no longer-range structure a wider kernel could have found.

The one directional positive. Per-punch cell-type-resolved LRIC g(r) for the two motif-1 pairs in both directions. The mGAM→MES-like curve for GRN→SORT1 sits above its reverse in 7 of 8 punches (medians 1.566 vs 1.410, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0156, the minimum attainable at n = 8); for ANXA1→FPR1 the two directions overlap (1.524 vs 1.560, p = 0.844). Note the spread across punches — this is why the single-punch benchmark was repeated across all 13.

Which sender the MOFA-Flex model actually spends its variance on. R² per factor per sender view: Glial-Neuronal dominates at 0.602 summed R², ahead of Vascular 0.399, MES-like 0.398, NPC-like 0.394, OPC-like 0.338 and AC-like 0.302. The two views that would carry motif 1 — mGAM and non-mGAM — are not on this plot at all: they were dropped by the tutorial's min_features=25 at 24 and 4 features.

Why the branch was run 13 times instead of once. The pooled whole-slide control against the per-punch medians, per annulus: pooling inflates LRIC g(r) 3.43× and cross-PCF 2.94× (against a 2.37× lower bound from bounding-box occupancy alone), and pushes the LRIC/cross-PCF ratio from ~1.0 to 1.21–1.28 for GRN→SORT1 and 1.74–2.26 for ANXA1→FPR1. A whole-slide run would have produced a false positive for exactly the claim under test.

LR-MISTy predictor importances for FPR1, the panel that carries both halves of this branch's verdict. Neighbourhood GRN is the 3rd strongest of 37 predictors (t = +7.08) — but ANXA1, the cognate ligand under test, sits at t = +1.34, rank 22 of 37, and does not replicate. C3 (+14.1) outranks everything, which is the shape of a niche-composition signal rather than a receptor-ligand one.

The five highest-|weight| sender^ligand^receptor features of each of the 20 MOFA-Flex factors, for the primary fit. Read this as the content of the programs the authors' prescribed route recovers on this slide — and note what is not in it: after the tutorial's own QC the feature pool is 419 features from 6 sender views, with every ANXA1^FPR1 feature and the whole mGAM view already removed.

uncertainties:
Things I could not verify, or that remain genuinely contested:

1. **Provenance of `--n-top-genes 1521` in the MISTy HVG probe.** It is a hardcoded default in `run_misty.py:103` with no recorded derivation in the script, DEVIATIONS.md or METHODS.md. The tutorial calls bare `sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata)`, which uses a dispersion cut and does NOT fix a gene count, so the probe approximates rather than reproduces the tutorial's HVG step. The measured collapse (382/37 -> 82/13 full slide, 54/1 on one punch) is real, but the exact numbers depend on this unexplained 1521.

2. **The 2,520-of-10,119,190 cross-core MISTy edge count.** Recorded in METHODS.md:53 and DEVIATIONS.md; I could not find the measuring script or its output file on disk, so I am relaying a documented number rather than one I recomputed. The 607.0 um nominal support, the 222.9 um inter-core floor, and the 99.7% cap-binding fraction I did verify (the last from the manifest's `conn_cap_binds_frac`).

3. **MOFA-Flex fit provenance is restored, not remeasured.** `fit_seconds` 4230/2022, `wall_seconds`, `peak_rss_gb` and the determinism probe were written back into the manifests from `logs/mofaflex_{primary,sensitivity}.log` after a replot nulled them. I independently confirmed the stopping epochs (`Training converged after 632 epochs` / `after 199 epochs` appear verbatim in those logs) but not the timings, which exist only as the restored values.

4. **Figures I wanted but could not propose.** `lric_percore/figures/direction_asymmetry_paired.png` (the cleanest single panel for the GRN->SORT1 asymmetry) and `grade_comparison_ratio.png` exist in `results/` but were NOT copied into `reports/liana_plus_GBM_cellchatdb2/`, and `mofaflex_inflow/plots/factor_by_punch_grade.png` likewise. The report tree holds only 5 LRIC PNGs of the 12 figure families produced. If the builder can reach `results/`, `lric/direction_asymmetry_paired.png` would be a better figure 2 than `gr_curves_per_punch.png`.

5. **Contested / judgement calls, flagged as such rather than resolved.**
   - CD-1 (the 13.1454 um bandwidth derived from ALARMIST's 50 um patch) is a deviation from our own benchmark contract and is **still OPEN, unsigned-off**. It applies to MOFA-Flex (which factorises an inflow object built at that bandwidth) but not to LRIC or LR-MISTy. Bandwidth alone moves the inflow NMF rank 11 -> 7, so any factor count from this branch is partly a function of a number imported from the method being compared against.
   - The sensitivity fit at `nzf > 0.001` is our deviation, not the tutorial's. Whether it is the right response to a QC that deletes the quantity under test, or whether the honest report is simply "the default pipeline cannot see it", is a judgement call. Both fits are on disk; neither was discarded.
   - Whether the punch-level Mann-Whitney should exist at all is contested: SKILL.md:49 says not to hand-roll a multi-sample mode. I report it as an additional analysis and mark the contract requirement N/A, but a stricter reading would omit it.
   - The MOFA-Flex sensitivity Factor 7 "myeloid-anchored loop" reading is weak and I have said so: F7 is only the 8th strongest factor for `mGAM^GRN^SORT1`. The concordant signs are real; the preference is not.

6. **Not independently re-derived by me:** the 42.2306% bbox occupancy and the two inflation factors (3.4284x / 2.9445x) come from the LRIC manifest's own `why_per_punch` block; I verified the bbox areas and the whole-slide-vs-per-punch ratio table but did not recompute the bounding boxes from coordinates.

title: What LIANA+ found — the biology
html:
What LIANA+ found — the biology

Ordered by how much a biologist would care, with the weakest claims marked as such.

NOTCH lateral induction inside the progenitor-like compartment

Inflow NMF Factor 7 is 50.6% NOTCH pathway by CellChatDB composition (ULM t = 9.73, FDR = 1.1×10−17) and is explicitly NPC-like–sourced: its top feature is NPC-like^DLL3^NOTCH1 at loading 21.50, sender fraction NPC-like 63.1% / OPC-like 13.7%. Bivariate Factor 6 is 55.5% NOTCH (top DLL3^NOTCH1, 8.35) and Factor 1 is 28.7% NOTCH (JAG1^NOTCH1, 13.83). In the source×target table the strongest edges are autocrine: OPC-like→OPC-like DLL3^NOTCH1 lr_mean = 1.682, NPC-like→NPC-like = 1.458, both p = 0.001. DLL3^NOTCH1 is also the 4th most spatially structured LR pair on the slide (Moran’s R = 0.0895).

This is the one program that survives every methodological choice we varied, which is the main reason to trust it.

Tumour → myeloid: APP→SORL1 and complement

The largest heterotypic edge on the slide is Glial-Neuronal→non-mGAM APP^SORL1 (lr_mean 1.224); into mGAM the same pair runs 0.43–0.63 from every tumour state. Then complement: MES-like→mGAM C4A^C3AR1 0.206 and C3^C3AR1 0.202, with a strong mGAM autocrine complement loop alongside. Counting only significant rows, Vascular (969) and mGAM (906) have the most incoming edges, against OPC-like (415).

The mGAM ↔ MES-like axis — and a correction

An earlier version of this analysis reported that LIANA corroborated only one arm of the ALARMIST motif-1 loop. That conclusion came from one branch (compute_global_specificity) and does not survive reading the others.

The spatially-constrained rank_aggregate — the standard-LR-methods leaf of the decision tree, 16,509 source×target×LR rows — supports both arms with the correct direction, and both reverse directions collapse:

Directionlr_meanslr_logfccellphone pmagnitude rank
mGAM → MES-like GRN→SORT10.914+0.9490.0000.0081
MES-like → mGAM ANXA1→FPR10.843+1.8840.0000.0124
MES-like → mGAM GRN→SORT1 (reverse)0.316−0.3121.0000.491
mGAM → MES-like ANXA1→FPR1 (reverse)0.293+0.046—0.705

The honest picture is that it depends which branch you ask:

  • rank_aggregate — both arms, correct direction, both reverses null.
  • compute_global_specificity — ANXA1→FPR1 rank 2 of 81 (p = 0.000999); GRN→SORT1 p = 1.00000.
  • LRIC, per punch — the GRN→SORT1 direction asymmetry holds (median g 1.566 forward vs 1.410 reverse, 7 of 8 punches, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.0156), but ANXA1→FPR1 does not replicate (1.524 vs 1.560, p = 0.844).
  • MISTy actively contradicts the ANXA1 arm: FPR1’s spatial neighbourhood is best explained by C3 (t = +14.1) and GRN (t = +7.1); ANXA1 ranks 22nd of 37 (t = +1.34).

So the directionality ALARMIST assigns to motif 1 is independently reproduced, most strongly for GRN→SORT1. The specific claim that ANXA1 is the ligand driving FPR1-high myeloid cells is the weaker half and is contradicted by the one multivariate method.

Distance says the co-occurrence is architectural, not expression-driven

LRIC divided by its cross-PCF baseline asks whether ligand/receptor expression adds anything over where the cells simply sit. Across 13 punches the ratio is ≈1 in essentially every distance bin out to 225 µm (per-punch medians 0.963–1.043; all one-sample Wilcoxon-vs-1 p > 0.10). The g(r) curve for GRN^SORT1 is flat, with no peak at any range.

This is a negative result and matters twice over: it says the mGAM/MES-like co-occurrence is explained by cell-type co-location alone, and it rules out the obvious defence that a 28.2 µm kernel simply missed a longer-range interaction.

Receptor expression is barely predictable from the ligand neighbourhood

Median gain_R² over 382 receptor targets is 0.0041; 133 exceed 0.01. The best target, MET (0.577), is reconstructed from THY1, TNR, TNC and NTN1 — its own cognate ligand HGF is absent from the model entirely, being non-zero in only 3.77% of cells. So where MISTy predicts well, it is reading mesenchymal/glial neighbourhood context, not ligand–receptor mechanism. Read GRN’s importance for SORT1 and FPR1 the same way.

Grade: nothing survives the correct replicate unit

Every cell-level grade contrast is significant and none of them should be believed as stated. Aggregating to the 13 punches (7 high vs 6 low) and applying Mann-Whitney + BH gives 0 of 7 NMF factors and 0 of 20 MOFA-Flex factors at q < 0.05; the smallest raw p is 0.014 against a two-sided floor of p = 0.0012 at n = 13. Two confounders compound this: the grade groups differ in composition (Glial-Neuronal 34% of low-grade cells vs 7% of high-grade), and one high-grade core supplies 26% of the slide. LRIC cannot test grade at all — 7 of the 8 punches with enough mGAM are high-grade, and the loss is systematic rather than random.

title: What LIANA+ cannot do that ALARMIST can
html:
What LIANA+ cannot do that ALARMIST can

Two of these are structural — they follow from how a feature is indexed and cannot be fixed by parameter choices. The rest follow from those two.

1. The feature is indexed differently, and it is not a notation difference

An ALARMIST feature is a 5-tuple (sender cell type, receiver cell type, ligand, receptor, contact mode) — 25,271 of them in this run: 81 ordered cell-type pairs × 712 LR pairs × 3 modes (15,544 paracrine / 7,610 juxtacrine / 2,117 autocrine). Each of the 20 motifs carries an independent weight on every one.

A LIANA inflow feature is (sender cell type, ligand, receptor). The receiver enters only through which cell the score is assigned to. So any NMF over inflow features factorises into a cell-loading margin and a (sender, LR) margin, and a (sender, receiver, LR) triple can only be reconstructed as an outer product of two margins.

Motif 1 falsifies that outer product directly. Within the single mGAM/MES-like cell pair:

MES-like|mGAM|ANXA1|FPR1|paracrine  = 92.79     mGAM|MES-like|ANXA1|FPR1|paracrine =  5.75
mGAM|MES-like|GRN|SORT1|paracrine   = 94.97     MES-like|mGAM|GRN|SORT1|paracrine  = 16.34

The two directional ratios are −4.01 and +5.81 in log2 — opposite biases, a 114-fold discrepancy, where an outer-product model requires a single constant. Across the 68 LR pairs present in both directions between those two cell types the log2 direction ratio spans −24.4 to +23.6 (sd 9.9), and several edges are strictly one-directional: CSF1→CSF1R, CX3CL1→CX3CR1, THY1→ITGAM_ITGB2 occur only MES-like→mGAM (exactly 0 in reverse), while WNT5A→FZD3, GAS6→TYRO3, HGF→MET occur only mGAM→MES-like.

So the “bidirectional loop” is not two symmetric halves — it is two chemically distinct arms, and LIANA’s factorisation cannot express that. Note also that ALARMIST’s plot_celltype_communication_by_motif pivots directly on (celltype1, celltype2) with no symmetrisation, so its 9×9 heatmap is an honest joint quantity rather than a product of two margins.

2. Downstream consequence: motif → gene

results/GBM/impact/ holds a Poisson GLM of raw counts on the z-scored log motif loading, fitted within each cell type: 20 motifs × 9 cell types = 180 tables, 266,746 gene tests. Critically, every tested gene is a non-ligand/receptor gene — the 593 LR symbols appearing in the feature names have zero overlap with the 2,435 genes tested for motif 1 in mGAM, so the readout is not circular.

Motif 1 in mGAM: CCL18 logFC 8.3, TGM2 4.7, MARCO 4.2 up; homeostatic-microglial P2RY12 and BHLHE41 down — a legible homeostatic-microglia → tumour-associated-macrophage transition.

LIANA does not attempt this. It speaks only inside the LR space. MISTy looks superficially similar but its targets are receptors drawn from the LR resource, not the transcriptome. Caveat, stated because it matters: 87% of ALARMIST’s GLM tests pass FDR, so these should be read by effect size rather than q-value, and the model has no overdispersion correction and no per-core random effect.

3. A per-cell program score to hang everything else on

ALARMIST projects its 20 patch-level motifs down to a 100,197 × 20 per-cell loading matrix. That matrix is the attachment point for GMM ON/OFF state calls, k-means motif niches, regression against the transcriptome, and motif-derived survival signatures. LIANA gives a score per cell per LR pair — there is no low-dimensional program score to attach anything to.

This one can be partly bolted on: run NMF on the inflow matrix, which we did. But the resulting factor is still (sender, LR)-indexed, so it inherits limitation 1. And empirically those factors are not communication programs — 6 of the 7 inflow factors are ≥75% a single sender, and 5 of 7 share the same top feature X^NCAM1^NCAM1, i.e. they largely encode cell-type identity plus one dominant adhesion pair.

4. Three smaller ones

  • Contact mode. ALARMIST features carry paracrine / juxtacrine / autocrine explicitly. LIANA uses one gaussian kernel and has no such axis.
  • Comparing two motifs that share a cell-type pair. Separating an mGAM motif from its near-identical non-mGAM twin is only a well-posed question when the feature is the full tuple; under a (sender, LR) feature set the two would be compared on the wrong axis.
  • Cross-dataset motif matching by cosine on the factor matrix, restricted to shared cell-type–LRI combinations. LIANA could only match on (sender, LR), so it structurally cannot detect the failure mode that matters most in practice: agreement at the gene and LR-pair level but disagreement about which cell type carries the interaction.

What LIANA has and ALARMIST does not

Stating the other direction, because the comparison is otherwise not useful:

  • Distance resolution. LRIC gives g(r) in 8 annuli out to 225 µm with a cross-PCF null to divide by. ALARMIST has a single patch scale and cannot ask whether an interaction is contact-range or diffusive.
  • Per-cell significance for a single LR pair, with permutation p-values and local high-high / low-low categories.
  • A multivariate, non-linear view (MISTy) asking how much of a target is explained by its whole spatial neighbourhood at once.
  • Method consensus — rank_aggregate combines CellPhoneDB, NATMI, Connectome, log2FC and others rather than relying on one statistic.

Finally, an honesty note: several analyses in ALARMIST’s documented toolbox — combinatorial motif-state programs, Hallmark/GSEA off motif states, motif-derived survival signatures — have no code and no outputs for this dataset. They are capabilities, not completed work, and should not be counted as demonstrated advantages here.
